Standard: Flight-critical sensors are connected directly to flight-critical computing. Inputs from sources not developed to flight-critical standards have dedicated monitors for health and validity which are developed to flight-critical standards and hosted on flight-critical hardware. Missing or erroneous sensor inputs from sources not developed to flight-critical standards do not result in exceeding air vehicle transient limits nor degrade the VCF below Operational State III. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Inspection of the VCF architecture shows flight-critical sensors connect directly to flight-critical computing without passing through non-flight-critical equipment.
(2) Inspection of the VCF architecture shows monitors of inputs from sources not developed to flight-critical standards are hosted on flight-critical hardware. Analysis.
  (1) Air vehicle transient analysis utilizing finalized monitor threshold and persistence values demonstrates transients are within air vehicle established limits. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct FMET SIL testing to verify monitor performance and associated transients.
    (2) Lab test: Pilot-in-the-loop simulations show that missing or erroneous data from non-flight-critical sources does not degrade the VCF below Operational State III.
